note.explanation: A dry run means following an algorithm manually with sample data. You track what happens at each step, including the values of variables and the output. This can help you spot logic errors before using a computer.
examples: For the addition flowchart, use A = 3 and B = 5: Sum = 3 + 5 = 8.
For FindMax, use num1 = 10 and num2 = 15: 10 > 15 is False, so max = 15.
note.checkAnswer: If num1 = 4 and num2 = 9, the output max is 9.
note.simple: A dry run is like acting out an algorithm by hand, one step at a time.
note.checkQuestion: If num1 = 4 and num2 = 9, what value does FindMax output?

written.text: Q7.9. Explain the concept of a dry run in the context of both flowcharts and pseudocode. How does performing a dry run help in validating the correctness of an algorithm?
written.finalAnswer: A dry run manually follows a flowchart step-by-step or simulates pseudocode line-by-line using sample data. It helps check the logic, variable values, decisions and output, so errors can be identified and the algorithm's correctness can be verified.

modelAnswer: A dry run of a flowchart involves manually walking through it step-by-step to understand how the algorithm works without using a computer.
A dry run of pseudocode involves manually simulating its execution line-by-line.

Check conditions and note how variable values change.
Check the output produced by the algorithm.
This helps verify the logic and correctness of the algorithm and identify errors.

explain.title: What a dry run is
explain.body: A dry run involves manually going through the algorithm with sample data to identify any errors.

explain.title: Dry running a flowchart
explain.body: A dry run of a flowchart involves manually walking through the flowchart step-by-step to understand how the algorithm works without using a computer. This helps identify any logical errors and understand the flow of control.

explain.title: Dry running pseudocode
explain.body: A dry run of pseudocode involves manually simulating the execution of the pseudocode line-by-line. This helps in verifying the logic and correctness of the algorithm.

explain.title: Simulation
explain.body: Simulation is we use of computer programs to create a model of a real-world process or system. This helps us understand how things work by testing different ideas or algorithms without needing to try them out in real life.

mistakes: Skipping a step in the flowchart or pseudocode instead of following the instructions in order.
Checking a condition incorrectly and then following the wrong branch.
Forgetting to update a variable after an assignment.
Writing the input values as the output without carrying out the calculation or comparison.
Giving only the final answer when the question asks you to show the dry run.
